title: Independent re-audit of the PLAY-04 audit fixes (findings 1/2 repaired; opening-phase residual R1)
actor: Claude Code agent (architect/QA reviewer role) on Director request, local WSL session

changes.description: Re-audited Codex commit bcaee09 (CHG-20261015-007) against the Director's four fix steps, audit findings 1 and 2, and the backlog acceptance (no disconnect/time abuse or duplicate terminal result). Reviewed the fix-only diff from 3753069: the early waiting-player refusal and waiting-concession deadline exemption in clock-store reserve, the BUSY service error, the gateway's rate_limited mapping, the stock client's retry handling, the nine regressions and the evidence runs RUN103-115 (failures 104-108 and 113 preserved and explained). Confirmed that the engine, bridge, migrations, public schemas and match client are unchanged.

Independent runs RUN-20261015-116..122 all passed at Codex's final fingerprint 0249c5a5 with exact timing, no clock discontinuity and 0 redactions. RUN116 full verify:foundation (350 project = 326 Node + 24 Python; 406 upstream/1 skip/1,362 expectations; 2 injection). RUN117 service probe on the real test database and engine with injected UTC: finding 1 repaired (waiting refusals do no engine work and change no clock revision or event; 8 turns with 24 concurrent waiting commands, every active pass accepted and the clock matching an independent model), busy contention retryable with no durable receipt, finding 2 repaired at and 3 s past the deadline with no timeout pass. RUN118/119 real gateway, database and time with stock clients. RUN120 boundary probe unchanged. RUN121 role health plus 74 database checks and db:check. RUN122 11 Chromium checks plus 2 Lab workers.

Finding R1 (Important, residual of finding 1): every waiting concession is exempt from the early refusal (clock-store.ts:82) and the deadline check (clock-store.ts:94-95), but the upstream opening flow accepts only chooseWhoGoesFirst/alterHand and forfeitGame (runtime-flow-config.ts:42,61), so the engine refuses every opening concession after it has taken the timed reservation. RUN117: 20 refused opening concessions, each about 170 ms of reservation, 2 clock revisions and 2 clock events; the active player's choice gets BUSY meanwhile. RUN118: with an opening concession holding the reservation, the stock client closes itself after 8 busy replies in 1.8 s (match-client index.ts:54). RUN119: repeated stock-client concessions in the opening, 18 steps over 8 matches, 15 with busy replies, active client closed in 6 of 8. Effect: the opening decision is blocked while the opening clock runs; expiry pauses the match for audited resume; no win or loss. Suggested fix: a waiting player's command never holds the timed reservation.

Observations: each refused opening concession writes one receipt and two clock events (about 11 events per second per waiting player at the measured speed); players cannot concede in the opening because the engine accepts only forfeitGame there (product question); finding 3 (real-card chooser) now also exists in the store's early refusal, still unreachable with synthetic cards; the four Director policy points remain open.

Validation re-audit section; ADR0016 re-audit note; runbook caution for R1; F-MATCH-CLOCKS description and evidence; FEATURES.md row; backlog PLAY-04 status implemented_audit_fixes_reaudited_residual_fix_required_before_merge; dated re-audit line after the shared PLAY-04 block in AGENTS.md, README.md and docs/README.md; handoff rewritten. Codex's records, executed evidence and the shared current block are unchanged.

limitations: Evidence is local Linux Dev Container and headless Chromium only; injected UTC in the service probe; no Windows, device, GPU, load, remote network or production observation.

RUN119 uses the stock client in a sequential loop; a custom client could hold the reservation more often. The closure rate depends on timing: RUN118's three-step repeated-concession section recorded no busy replies, while RUN119 closed the active client in 6 of 8 matches.
Local isolated CI was not rerun (wall clock drifts against monotonic); hosted CI on the fix source follows publication and is recorded in a later change.
